rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with an expanded blastocyst and strong ICM/looser TE, but it overstates thinning/pre-hatching and mentions subtle fragmentation/debris not clearly supported by the image.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor diagnosis, BMI, sperm parameters, endometrium, cycle history, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, linking embryo grade and favorable patient factors to prognosis; probability estimate is plausible though somewhat optimistic.

Generally aligned with Gardner grading interpretation and standard IVF practice, including support for single embryo transfer in a good-prognosis 33-year-old; minor overinterpretation of morphology prevents a perfect score.
Provides a clear recommendation for SET and general transfer planning, but the future-cycle guidance is truncated and lacks fuller practical detail or contingency planning.
